title: audit-llama-runtime-state
summary: Audit llama.cpp context memory, partial decode progress, graph reuse and server cancellation when a retry, stale prefix, unexpected rebuild or unreleased slot needs an ownership explanation; requires pinned source or a concrete runtime trace.

skill_metadata.name: audit-llama-runtime-state
skill_metadata.description: Audit llama.cpp context memory, partial decode progress, graph reuse and server cancellation when a retry, stale prefix, unexpected rebuild or unreleased slot needs an ownership explanation; requires pinned source or a concrete runtime trace.

applicability.scope: Pinned llama.cpp context-memory, graph-reuse and server task-lifecycle diagnosis; concrete model/backend behavior requires native validation.
applicability.prerequisites: Pinned llama.cpp source or a concrete runtime trace, access to the relevant memory/graph/server ownership evidence and an identified caller recovery policy that remains in force.
applicability.input_contract: Source/build and model revisions, memory type, actual backend/device and execution mode, context/batch/ubatch parameters, sequence IDs/positions/output flags and return status; graph cases need dispatch evidence, server cases need correlated HTTP/task/slot/cache logs.
applicability.produced_artifact: An owner/event ledger of ubatch progress, retained memory, graph-gate decisions, input readiness and slot release/retention, with the first supported broken obligation or smallest missing observation.
applicability.failure_modes: Assuming whole-batch rollback after partial decode failure, treating token count as a complete graph-reuse key, or equating posted cancellation with released slots can hide retained state or misdiagnose correct deferred work.
applicability.refusal_point: Stop before reset or repair if revision, memory type, actual backend, sequence ownership or partial progress is unknown; escalate unsupported rollback or unresolved in-flight work.

limitations: Source-derived candidate; native runtime and efficacy validation not run.
No cross-backend preemption, model-quality or performance claim.
KV, recurrent and hybrid state contracts must be checked independently.
recommendations: Reconcile per-sequence retained positions with completed ubatches before retrying a failed logical batch.
Check both graph allow_reuse and input can_reuse gates, then establish copy readiness independently of graph identity.
Trace cancellation posting, normal task processing, slot release and prompt retention as separate events.
